7-source-2.title: Joint Technical Standards on major incident reporting
7-source-2.applicability: All financial entities subject to DORA incident reporting requirements

passages.text: The draft RTS set out time limits for reporting of the initial notification of 4 hours after classification and 24 hours after detection of the incident, 72 hours for reporting of the intermediate report and 1 month for the reporting of the final report.

7-source-3.title: DORA Incident Reporting – Operational Instructions
7-source-3.applicability: Competent authorities and financial entities reporting under DORA Article 19

passages.text:
This document provides operational instructions intended to support competent authorities in their supervisory engagement with financial entities
regarding the reporting of information on the major ICT-related incidents under Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 (DORA)

concerns.description: Financial entities must report major ICT-related incidents to competent authorities through a single streamlined framework as required by DORA Article 19.
Payment service providers must report operational or security payment-related incidents under DORA, replacing previous incident reporting requirements under Directive (EU) 2015/2366.

Time limits for incident reporting: initial notification within 4 hours after classification (and 24 hours after detection), intermediate report within 72 hours, and final report within one month after the intermediate report as specified in RTS 2025/301.

Financial entities may voluntarily notify significant cyber threats to competent authorities when threats are relevant to the financial system, service users, or clients as permitted under DORA Article 19.
Operational instructions support competent authorities in supervising financial entities' reporting of major ICT-related incidents to enhance data quality and consistency across jurisdictions.
